title: Building Interactive Widgets with RserveTS
text: Widgets RserveTS stateful objects can shared R TypeScript applications. provide: Reactive properties: Properties automatically synchronize R TypeScript Property handlers: Callbacks trigger properties change Hierarchical structure: Widgets can contain child widgets Type safety: Full TypeScript type definitions generated R code

title: Building Interactive Widgets with RserveTS
text: example application demonstrates three interconnected widgets working iris dataset: Plot Control Widget (CtrlWidget): controller widget coordinates histogram barchart widgets Histogram Widget (HistogramWidget): Displays histogram selected variable interactive bar selection Barplot Widget (BarchartWidget): Shows species counts update based row selection

title: Building Interactive Widgets with RserveTS
text: histogram widget allows users select variable number bins, displays resulting histogram. also supports interactive selection histogram bars filter data. Key features: Properties defined using ts_*() functions specify TypeScript types initialize function sets initial state property handlers Property handlers (addPropHandler) trigger callbacks properties change update() method recalculates histogram synchronizes state updateState() pushes changes TypeScript frontend
code: histogramWidget <- createWidget(     "HistogramWidget",     properties = list(         vars = ts_character(0L),           # Available variable names         var = ts_character(1L),             # Currently selected variable         nBin = ts_integer(1L),              # Number of bins         counts = ts_numeric(0L),            # Histogram counts         selectedBar = ts_integer(1L),      # Currently selected bar index         controller = "ANY"                 # Parent controller widget     ),     initialize = function(widget, parent = NULL) {         # Assign parent to controller property         if (!is.null(parent)) {             widget$controller <- parent         }          # Initialize available variables (excluding Species)         allvars <- names(iris)         widget$set("vars", allvars[allvars != "Species"])         widget$set("var", "")         widget$set("nBin", 10L)         widget$set("selectedBar", 0L)         widget$set("counts", numeric(0))          # Initial update         widget$update()          # Set up property handlers for reactive updates         widget$addPropHandler("var", function() widget$update())         widget$addPropHandler("nBin", function() widget$update())          # Handle bar selection to filter data         if (!is.null(widget$controller)) {             widget$addPropHandler("selectedBar", function() {                 x <- iris[[widget$var]]                 if (widget$selectedBar < 0) {                     widget$controller$set("selectedRows", seq_along(x))                     return()                 }                 br <- hist(x,                     seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = widget$nBin + 1L),                     plot = FALSE                 )$breaks                 i <- widget$selectedBar + 1                 xx <- which(x >= br[i] & x < br[i + 1])                 widget$controller$set("selectedRows", xx)             })         }     },     methods = list(         update = ts_function(             function() {                 if (.self$var == "") {                     return()                 }                 x <- iris[[.self$var]]                 h <- hist(x,                     seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = .self$nBin + 1L),                     plot = FALSE                 )                  # Update the front end                 .self$set("counts", as.numeric(h$counts))                  # Push changes through to UI                 .self$updateState()             }         )     ),     export = TRUE )

title: Building Interactive Widgets with RserveTS
text: barplot widget displays species counts updates based row filtering controller. Key features: Uses ts_dataframe() define structured data typed columns Automatically updates subset property changes update() method recalculates counts filtered data
code: barchartWidget <- createWidget(     "BarchartWidget",     properties = list(         data = ts_dataframe(label = ts_character(0L), count = ts_integer(0L)),         subset = ts_integer()  # Row indices to include     ),     initialize = function(widget) {         widget$set("subset", seq_len(nrow(iris)))         widget$update()         widget$addPropHandler("subset", function() widget$update())     },     methods = list(         update = ts_function(             function() {                 tbl <- xtabs(~Species, data = iris[.self$subset, ]) |>                     as.data.frame() |>                     setNames(c("label", "count"))                  .self$set("data", tbl)                 .self$updateState()             }         )     ),     export = TRUE )

title: Typed Application Contracts for Rserve
text: Writing functions easy, just use ts_*() functions define formals return types. use ts_compile() generate TypeScript schemas: can import rserve-ts application. See tests/testthat/sampler example.
code: # demo.R library(RserveTS) addFn <- ts_function(   function(a = ts_numeric(1), b = ts_numeric(1)) a + b,   result = ts_numeric(1) ) sampleFn <- ts_function(   function(x = ts_character(), n = ts_integer(1)) sample(x, n),   result = ts_character() ) app <- ts_function(   function() {     list(       add = addFn,       sample = sampleFn     )   },   result = ts_list(     add = addFn,     sample = sampleFn   ) ) import { Robj } from 'rserve-ts'; import { z } from 'zod';  const addFn = Robj.ocap([z.number(), z.number()], Robj.numeric(1)); const app = Robj.ocap([],   Robj.list({     add: Robj.ocap(),     sample: Robj.ocap()   }) ); const sampleFn = Robj.ocap(   [z.union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())]), z.number()],   Robj.character() );  export default {   addFn,   app,   sampleFn };

title: Typed Application Contracts for Rserve
text: Generated .ts files single long line per export default. npm available, install Prettier app project (recommended: dev dependency) npx prettier works directory: prettier npx PATH, pass format = TRUE compiling file: can point specific formatter prettier_cmd (full argv, executable first), R option RserveTS.prettier_cmd, environment variable RserveTS_PRETTIER_CMD (space-separated tokens). package writes generated source temporary .ts file runs command path last argument, Prettier prettier file.ts. Another CLI (e.g. Biome) can used supports “format file path” pattern. also possible generate sourceable file deploy Rserve instance app code using ts_deploy():
code: npm install --save-dev prettier ts_compile("app.R", filename = "app.rserve", format = TRUE) ts_deploy(app) # run with: Rscript app.rserve.R

title: Create 'TypeScript'-compatible widgets — createWidget
code: widgetActions(..., strict = "warn", enabled = TRUE)  createWidget(   name,   properties = list(),   initialize = NULL,   methods = list(),   actions = FALSE,   auto_flush = TRUE,   .env = parent.frame(),   ... )  observer(props, fn)

title: Create 'TypeScript'-compatible widgets — createWidget
text: ... createWidget(): passed underlying ts_function() constructor. widgetActions(): named ts_function() action definitions. strict widgetActions(): unknown action handling ("", "warn", "strict"). enabled widgetActions(): whether action support enabled. name Widget class name (character). properties Named list typed properties (ts_*() objects, nested widget constructors). initialize Optional function run defaults applied; receives widget instance parameter. methods Named list ts_function() methods /observer() reactive methods. actions FALSE/TRUE, list enabled/types/strict, widgetActions() object. auto_flush TRUE (default), methods flush state 'TypeScript' return; FALSE, call updateState() manually. .env Environment ref class definition (default parent.frame()). props observer(): property names trigger method. fn observer(): method body (function ts_function()).

title: Create 'TypeScript'-compatible widgets — createWidget
text: widget instances inherit tsWidget include: set(prop, value), get(prop) – field access change tracking updateState(= FALSE) – push changed properties 'TypeScript' addPropHandler(prop, fn) – react property changes batch(props, expr) – batch updates one state flush add_child(property, widget_def) – attach nested widget create_dynamic_child(widget_def) – runtime child widget destroy() – tear widget

title: Create 'TypeScript'-compatible widgets — createWidget

Obtain widget Ocaps compiled app schema (example app.histogram connecting useRserve() React). React, useWidget() @tmelliott/react-rserve wraps compiled widget constructor keeps 'JavaScript' state sync R: state – current property values (R updateState()) set – update properties client methods – call exported ts_function() methods widget children – nested widget connectors properties include child widgets Action-enabled widgets (actions = widgetActions(...)) also expose capabilities, dispatchAction, undo, redo hook return value.

code: Counter <- createWidget(     name = "Counter",     properties = list(count = ts_integer(1L, default = 0L)),     methods = list(         increment = ts_function(function(by = ts_integer(1L)) {             .self$count <- as.integer(.self$count + by)             .self$count         }, result = ts_integer(1)),         on_count = observer("count", function() NULL)     ) ) inherits(Counter, "ts_widget") #> [1] TRUE ts_compile(Counter) #> export const Counter = Robj.ocap( #>   [ #>     z.union([ #>       Robj.js_function( #>         [z.object({ count: z.union([z.number(), z.undefined()]) })], #>         z.null(), #>       ), #>       z.undefined(), #>     ]), #>   ], #>   Robj.list({ #>     properties: Robj.list({ #>       count: Robj.list({ #>         register: Robj.ocap( #>           [Robj.js_function([z.number()], z.null()), z.string()], #>           Robj.character(1), #>         ), #>         get: Robj.ocap([], Robj.integer(1)), #>         set: Robj.ocap([z.number()], Robj.null()), #>       }), #>     }), #>     children: Robj.list(), #>     capabilities: Robj.list({ #>       actions: Robj.list({ #>         enabled: Robj.logical(1), #>         types: Robj.character(0), #>         strict: Robj.character(1), #>       }), #>     }), #>     methods: Robj.list({ increment: Robj.ocap([z.number()], Robj.integer(1)) }), #>   }), #> );

title: Compile R functions — ts_compile
text: f function file path (length-one character string file compilation). ... Additional arguments. file path method, named arguments passed ts_deploy() (e.g. init, port, run). ts_function() / ts_widget objects, format prettier_cmd supported (see details); arguments ignored.

title: Compile R functions — ts_compile
text: ts_function() / ts_widget, character string 'TypeScript'. file path, writes .ts / .R beside filename returns output base path invisibly.

title: Compile R functions — ts_compile
text: ts_function() method: name defaults deparse(substitute(f)) sets generated export const symbol. Character (file) method: filename base path output; .R .ts extensions appended. omitted, output goes default compile directory (see ) {basename(f)}.rserve. Arguments filename, format, prettier_cmd must passed name; part .... Default output directory (CRAN-safe; write beside source default): option RserveTS.compile_dir set non-empty path; else environment variable RSERVETS_COMPILE_DIR set; else tempdir(). local development, set e.g. options(RserveTS.compile_dir = ".") RSERVETS_COMPILE_DIR=. ts_compile("app.R") writes app.rserve.ts / app.rserve.R working directory; pass filename explicitly. format – TRUE, run 'Prettier' (compatible CLI) generated 'TypeScript' (returned string functions; written .ts files). Defaults getOption("RserveTS.format", FALSE) can enable session (e.g. 'pkgdown' site builds) without changing call sites. prettier_cmd – Character vector argv (executable first). Defaults getOption("RserveTS.prettier_cmd") (NULL set , e.g. options(RserveTS.prettier_cmd = c("prettier", "--parser", "typescript"))). still NULL, falls back environment variable RserveTS_PRETTIER_CMD (space-separated tokens), prettier npx prettier PATH. temporary .ts copy generated source appended last argument (prettier --parser typescript path//file.ts). Another formatter (e.g. 'Biome') can used accepts invocation pattern.

title: Compile R functions — ts_compile
code: # Compile a typed function to a 'TypeScript' schema string (no files written) f <- ts_function(function(x = ts_integer(1)) x + 1L, result = ts_integer(1)) ts_compile(f) #> export const f = Robj.ocap([z.number()], Robj.integer(1));  # File compilation writes under tempdir() by default (or RSERVETS_COMPILE_DIR) src <- tempfile(fileext = ".R") writeLines(     "add <- ts_function(function(x = ts_integer(1)) x + 1L, result = ts_integer(1), export = TRUE)",     src ) out <- ts_compile(src) file.exists(paste0(out, ".ts")) #> [1] TRUE file.exists(paste0(out, ".R")) #> [1] TRUE
